name: Servants
overview: Scripture presents servants as individuals bound in submission and service within various relational contexts, as seen when Abram armed his trained servants to rescue his kin, demonstrating loyalty and readiness (Genesis 14:14). The narrative of Hagar instructs servants to submit under their masters' authority (Genesis 16:9), highlighting the expected obedience in these roles. Additionally, the strife between herdsmen in Genesis 13:7 and Abram's direction to Sarai regarding her maid (Genesis 16:6) reflect the complex social dynamics involving servants. These passages collectively show servants as integral to household and societal functions, operating under the authority of their masters while fulfilling vital duties.
